name: Rufous-tailed Flatbill
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, northern bolivia, and amazonian brazil
description: Smallish flycatcher, characteristic of forests on sandy soils and seasonally flooded forests. Heard more often than seen.

name: Black-chested Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Wetar (lesser sundas)
description: An unmistakable, strikingly patterned songbird with a downcurved bill. Olive above, with a conspicuous white throat bordered below by a necklace of dark streaks.

name: Falcated Duck
rangeDescription: Breeds mongolia, eastern siberia, and northeastern china; winters northern india to southern and eastern china, southern korean peninsula, and japan
description: An East Asian teal-like duck. Males are distinctive, with an iridescent head that flashes green and copper, a silvery body with distinct scalloping, extremely long curved tertials, long pale scapulars, and a triangular white throat patch outlined in dark green.

name: Bradfield's Hornbill
rangeDescription: Northwestern zimbabwe to southwestern zambia, northern botswana, and southern angola
description: Brown hornbill with a white belly and an orange bill. The white corners of the tail are conspicuous in flight.

name: Petit's Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Southeastern nigeria and cameroon to northeastern democratic republic of the congo, western uganda, and western kenya
description: A forest-dwelling cuckooshrike in which males and females are strikingly different. Males are entirely black with a greenish gloss.

name: Arabian Waxbill
rangeDescription: Southwestern arabian peninsula
description: A mostly gray-and-buff barred waxbill with a crimson ‘bandit’s’ eye-patch and black tail and rump. A predominantly gray waxbill with buff-washed underparts and fine barring all over the body, as well as a crimson “bandit’s” eye-patch and black tail and rump.

name: Common Bronzewing
rangeDescription: Australia including tasmania
description: A plump, attractive brown pigeon with beautiful green and bronze iridescent coloration in the wings. Males have a bright yellow and white forehead that is absent in females.

name: Magellanic Oystercatcher
rangeDescription: South-central chile and argentina to cape horn archipelago and falkland islands
description: A boldly patterned large and chunky shorebird of southern South America and Falklands. Favors rocky coastlines and adjacent river mouths, but also frequent on nearby grasslands and lakeshores.

name: Chestnut Seedeater
rangeDescription: Paraguay to south-central brazil, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Handsome seedeater. Males are mostly chestnut with a gray cap, wings, and tail, while females are sandy-colored and difficult to separate from other female seedeaters.

name: Vegetarian Finch
rangeDescription: Main islands of galapagos (except for more arid islands)
description: A large and rather parrot-billed Galápagos finch. Bill is about as long as it is deep, with a very round upper edge and slightly curved lower edge.

name: Olive-backed Forest Robin
rangeDescription: Not well known, but reported in southwestern gabon south of the ogooué river and, in northeastern gabon, north of the ogooué river
description: Localized species found only in lowland rainforest south of the River Ogooué in Gabon, and possibly also in adjacent Congo. A short-tailed understory robin with a bright orange throat.

name: Club-winged Manakin
rangeDescription: West slope of andes of southwestern colombia and western ecuador
description: Unique and entertaining manakin found in lush cloud forest in western Ecuador and western Colombia. Wine-red, black, and white male is unlike any other species in range.

name: Somali Starling
rangeDescription: Eritrea and ethiopia to northern somalia, abd el kuri island, and socotra
description: A large glossy-black starling with a strong bill. The very long and pointed tail and large red wing panels are conspicuous in flight.

name: Hooded Grebe
rangeDescription: Breeds submontane lakes of western santa cruz province, southwestern argentina; winters to río santa cruz estuary and adjacent coast, southeastern argentina
description: A beautiful, small grebe of Patagonia that is rare, local, and declining; breeds on a few interior lakes. Nonbreeding birds range to coastal waters and lowland lakes, where they are most often seen in the company of Silvery Grebes.

name: Festive Coquette
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (espírito santo, minas gerais, and santa catarina)
description: Tiny hummingbird with a white rump band found in the Atlantic Rainforest region. Adult male has a fantastic iridescent green headdress consisting of a flowing beard ending in white spots, and a glittering face and forehead.

name: Mewing Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Mangroves of mangaia island (southern cook islands)
description: A chunky, large-billed kingfisher with a greenish crown, cheek, and back and bluish wings and tail. White underneath with a strongly orange wash to the eyebrow and neck.

name: Inambari Gnatcatcher
rangeDescription: Western amazonian brazil south of the amazon river and west of the rio madeira
description: Recently described, inconspicuous and rarely seen bird of rainforest canopy. Small and slender with a long tail; mostly dark gray with a broken white eyering, white belly, and white outer tail feathers.

name: Marvelous Spatuletail
rangeDescription: Andes of northern peru (along east bank of río utcubamba)
description: Celebrated hummingbird restricted to Andean cloud forest in northern Peru. With his outrageous tail, blue crown, and iridescent green throat, the male ranks as one of the world’s most spectacular birds.

name: Eared Pitta
rangeDescription: Bangladesh to myanmar, thailand, southern china, southern cambodia, and central annam
description: This handsome pitta is about the color of a chocolate chip cookie. Only the warmer-colored male is “eared”, possessing the speckled silvery tufts on either side of the head.

name: Black Oystercatcher
rangeDescription: Western aleutians to central baja california and los coronados islands
description: Large, bulky shorebird. Dark overall with thick red bill, staring yellow eye, and thick, light pink legs.
